# Incident Report: Network Packet Capture Analysis
**Evidence file:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 packets, capture duration 3,202 sec / ~53 min)
**Analysis tool:** tshark 4.x
**No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory** — this report is based on manual protocol analysis of the raw capture only.

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** |
| AD domain | bluemoontuesday.com |
| Logged-in Windows user | **shutchenson** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `shutchenson` and `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ$`) |

Identified via DHCP Request (Option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ`, offered IP 10.1.17.215), corroborated by NBNS name registrations and Kerberos traffic to the domain controller (10.1.17.2 / WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com).

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/IDS detection names were present in the evidence (no Suricata/AV logs were provided), so this is based purely on traffic behavior:

- **Initial access technique: ClickFix** (fake verification/CAPTCHA social-engineering page tricking the user into pasting and running an attacker-supplied command via the Windows Run dialog). This is a well-established, recognizable pattern.
- **Payload behavior:** a VBScript "component" (HTA-style dropper) launches hidden PowerShell, which runs a self-decoding Base64/EncodedCommand loader. The decoded PowerShell computes the C:\ volume serial number as a bot ID and enters an infinite `DownloadString` / `Invoke-Expression` polling loop against the C2 — a generic **PowerShell RAT/backdoor loader** pattern, not tied to one named commodity family by traffic alone.
- The C2 subsequently pushed commands to create a persistence shortcut and to launch a legitimate **TeamViewer** client (downloaded components `TV`, `TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`) for hands-on-keyboard remote access — a "tech-support-scam"/RAT abuse-of-legitimate-RMM pattern.
- A separate, custom TLS channel to `45.125.66.32:2917` using a self-signed certificate (CN = "45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate") functioned as a second backdoor/C2 channel, reconnecting repeatedly over the session.

I cannot assign a specific named malware family (e.g., a commodity stealer/RAT brand) with confidence without external threat-intel lookup, which was excluded from this analysis per instructions. Everything below is grounded directly in the capture.

## Timeline of Compromise (relative to capture start, t=0)
1. **t≈38s** — DNS/TLS to `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (104.21.x.x, Cloudflare-fronted) — fake verification lure page.
2. **t≈38.8–39.5s** — DNS/TLS to `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — ClickFix payload/fingerprinting infrastructure.
3. **t≈52.3–52.7s** — DNS/TLS to `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109) — final lure stage, immediately preceding the malicious download.
4. **t=60.30s** — `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — victim pulls a VBScript "component" (HTA-style dropper).
5. **t=60.30s onward** — dropper launches hidden PowerShell that opens `https://azure.microsoft.com` (decoy tab) and downloads `http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1`.
6. **t=60s to t=3202s (end of capture)** — infected host polls `http://5.252.153.241/<disk-serial>` (e.g. `/1517096937`) every ~5 seconds, **584 beacon requests** observed over the full capture, receiving further obfuscated PowerShell to execute (`Invoke-Expression`). Observed C2 status callbacks from the malware itself:
   - `?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;`
   - `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`
7. **t≈611s** — legitimate TeamViewer traffic begins (`master16.teamviewer.com`, `185.188.32.26`, `din.aspx?...client=DynGate`) — consistent with the attacker deploying TeamViewer for interactive remote control, driven by the C2-issued "RunRH" command.
8. **t≈889s onward** — repeated short TLS sessions to `45.125.66.32:2917` using a self-signed certificate — secondary custom C2/backdoor channel, reconnecting at least 9 times through the end of the capture.

## Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-Control Endpoints (IP:port)
| Endpoint | Role |
|---|---|
| **5.252.153.241:80** | Primary stager/C2 — hosts dropper and PS payloads, receives disk-serial beacon polling (HTTP, plaintext) |
| **45.125.66.32:2917** | Secondary C2/backdoor — TLS 1.2, self-signed cert (CN "45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate"), non-standard port, repeated short reconnects |

### Malicious/Lure Domains
| Domain | Resolved IP | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` | 104.21.64.1 (and other Cloudflare anycast) | ClickFix fake "Google Authenticator" verification lure |
| `authenticatoor.org` | 82.221.136.26 | ClickFix payload/lure infrastructure |
| `appointedtimeagriculture.com` | 217.70.186.109 | Final ClickFix lure stage, immediately precedes payload download |

Note: `5.252.153.241` and `45.125.66.32` were contacted by raw IP (no DNS lookup preceded either), so no C2 domain names could be extracted for those two endpoints.

### Malicious URLs
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — VBScript dropper component
- `http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell downloader/RAT loop
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — duplicate/alternate copy of the PowerShell loader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`, `.../TeamViewer`, `.../Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — legitimate TeamViewer binaries staged for attacker use
- `http://5.252.153.241/<disk-serial>` (e.g. `/1517096937`) — beaconing/tasking URL, unique per infected host (bot ID = victim's C:\ volume serial number)

### Transferred Files and SHA-256 Hashes
| File | Size | SHA-256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `264872` | 417 bytes | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` | VBScript component: launches hidden PowerShell, opens decoy `azure.microsoft.com` tab, downloads/executes `29842.ps1` |
| `29842.ps1` | 1,512 bytes | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` | Obfuscated PowerShell: computes disk volume serial as bot ID, loops `DownloadString`/`Invoke-Expression` against `http://5.252.153.241/<serial>` every 5s |
| `pas.ps1` | 1,553 bytes | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` | Same decoded payload/logic as `29842.ps1` (duplicate stage) |
| `TV` | 12,920 bytes | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` | PE32 DLL, TeamViewer component, staged for attacker remote-access deployment |
| `TeamViewer` | 4,380,968 bytes | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` | TeamViewer main client executable, downloaded and executed on victim host |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` | 668,968 bytes | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` | TeamViewer French language resource, part of the same deployment |

## Bottom Line
DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, user shutchenson) was compromised via a ClickFix-style fake-verification page (`appointedtimeagriculture.com` chain), which led to execution of a VBScript dropper (`264872`) and a self-decoding PowerShell backdoor (`29842.ps1`/`pas.ps1`) that beaconed to `5.252.153.241` using the machine's disk serial number as a bot ID. The attacker used this channel to push a persistence shortcut, deploy a real TeamViewer client for hands-on remote access, and maintain a second self-signed-TLS backdoor to `45.125.66.32:2917`. Malware family attribution is behavioral only — no signature/AV confirmation was available in the provided evidence.
